---
title: "Min–max polyline decimation"
format: html
---

## Overview

`CorePlotting::decimatePolyLineBatchMinMax()` reduces the number of vertices in each line strip of a `RenderablePolyLineBatch` by **uniform x-binning** and keeping the **minimum and maximum y** in each bin (plus the first and last original vertices). This matches common oscilloscope-style downsampling for time series when the horizontal resolution is far smaller than the sample count.

**Location:** `src/CorePlotting/LineDecimation/MinMaxPolylineDecimation.hpp` (declaration), `.cpp` (implementation).

## Parameters

- `MinMaxDecimationParams::bucket_count`: number of x-buckets along each line. **`0` disables** decimation (identity).
- If a strip has at most `2 * bucket_count + 2` vertices, it is passed through unchanged.

## Integration

- **DataViewer** sets `AnalogBatchParams::min_max_decimation_bucket_count` from the widget width (clamped) when the per-series option `AnalogSeriesOptionsData::enable_min_max_line_decimation` is true. `DataViewerHelpers::buildAnalogSeriesBatchSimplified` / `buildAnalogSeriesBatchCached` call the decimator after vertices are assembled.
- **PlottingOpenGL** and **PlottingSVG** consume the same `RenderablePolyLineBatch`; no renderer changes are required.

## Degenerate x-span

When the first and last x of a strip are equal (or nearly equal), bucketing falls back to **index-based** bins so vertical stacks of samples still decimate.
